# OCC: 🟡Omarchy Control Center Implementation Plan

**Spec:** [`docs/OCC_SPECIFICATION.md`](docs/OCC_SPECIFICATION.md). **Decisions:** [`docs/OCC_DECISIONS.md`](docs/OCC_DECISIONS.md). **Agent rules:** [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md). **Shared phase instructions:** [`prompts/OCC_shared-instructions.md`](prompts/OCC_shared-instructions.md)
**Last updated:** 2026-10-21 11:09 CDT (phase 08 complete)

> ⚠️ **Mandatory:** every agent that works on this project keeps this file accurate. **Before doing any other work, set your phase to `🔄 In progress` and commit that change to `main`** (claim protocol: `prompts/OCC_shared-instructions.md` §1a). Other agents read this table from `main`. At the end, set it to `✅ Complete` or `⛔ Blocked` and add a Phase Log entry. See `CLAUDE.md`.

## How to run a phase
Open Claude Code in `/home/nick/Work/OCC_OmarchyControlCenter` and type one of:
- `/phase`: run the next eligible phase. It checks dependencies, tells you if you're on the wrong model, resumes an `In progress` phase, and asks about any open questions it needs.
- `/phase NN`: run a specific phase.
- `/phase status`: show progress and what's next, without doing any work.
- `/phase-add [after NN] <request>`: plan a new lettered phase (`09a`) later; it never builds.

Review the agent's close-out summary, then merge the phase branch when satisfied.

Each phase is claimed by a `chore(plan): start phase NN` commit on `main` and runs in its own worktree, `../OCC_OmarchyControlCenter-phase-NN`, so parallel sessions never share a checkout. `/phase status` flags any branch or worktree whose row is not `🔄 In progress`.

**Parallelism:** after Phase 04, phases **05** and **06** can run in parallel (05 touches `config/` and `internal/service` catalogue code plus the vault; 06 touches `internal/server`, `internal/lifecycle`, `internal/theme`). After Phase 06, **07** and **08** can run in parallel with each other (and with 05 if it is still running): 07 owns `cmd/`, `internal/voice`, `scripts/` and the host bind; 08 owns `web/`. Phase 09 waits for 05, 07 and 08.

**Status values:** ⬜ Not started · 🔄 In progress · ⛔ Blocked · ✅ Complete. Always write the icon **and** the word.

### Model rationale
- **Opus 5.5** (`/model claude-opus-5-5`) where a mistake is subtle or costly: the config/status core (state classification and parsing, phase 03), the adapters that drive systemd and `/proc` and must never touch the wrong unit (04), the live service integration with its RClone/Ollama/MM3 edge cases (05), the server's security middleware, locking and lifecycle state machine (06), the complex interactive dashboard UI (08), and the security review (11).
- **Sonnet 5.5** (`/model claude-sonnet-5-5`) for well-specified work: governance files (01), scaffolding and CI (02), the launcher/voice/bind integration whose design is fixed in R10-R16 (07), polish on an existing base (09), docs and templates (10), and release packaging (12).

### Dependency graph
```
00 ─► 01 ─► 02 ─► 03 ─► 04 ─┬─► 05 ───────────────┐
                            │                      │
                            └─► 06 ─┬─► 07 ────────┼─► 09 ─► 10 ─► 11 ─► 12
                                    │              │
                                    └─► 08 ────────┘
Parallel windows: {05, 06} after 04;  {05, 07, 08} after 06.
07a (quit key) follows 07, can run beside 08 or 09, and must be done before 12.
```

### Definition of done (checked in the final phase)
- [ ] `Super + Alt + T` → Prometheus-voice "OCC is starting" in < 300 ms and the dashboard window visible in < 2 s (measured, R18).
- [ ] Pressing it again → "OCC is already running" and the existing window is focused; no second server process.
- [ ] Quit key: `Super + Alt + Shift + T` quits OCC (cue, stopped screen, window closed) and is harmless when OCC is not running (Phase 07a).
- [ ] Each of the five services shows Healthy / Distressed / Stopped / Unavailable correctly, with CPU, memory and uptime, refreshed at 5 s-10 m (default 10 s) plus a manual refresh.
- [ ] Start / Stop / Restart work for all five; started services keep running after OCC quits; RClone autostart still works after a reboot (never enabled/disabled).
- [ ] MM3 Busy and Ollama-consumer confirmations appear before disruptive actions.
- [ ] Open WebUI shows container CPU/memory, Open focuses its window, Stop closes it, and `Super + Alt + O` still works unchanged.
- [ ] Quit → "OCC is stopping", a friendly "OCC stopped" screen, OCC's process gone in < 2 s, every managed service in the state it was in.
- [ ] Colours follow the active Omarchy theme; the Tron look holds on nx-protocol and on one other installed theme.
- [ ] Missing launcher/unit shows Unavailable with a reason; port conflicts fall back and are announced.
- [ ] Log viewer works for every service with a log source.
- [ ] Security baseline S1-S10 verified; threat model written; scanners clean.
- [ ] Adding a fifth service needs only a config block (demonstrated in Phase 10).
- [ ] Not running: zero processes, zero timers.
- [ ] OSMods README and write-up current; vault note current; repository GitHub-ready.

### 2026-10-20 19:37 CDT: Planning: Open WebUI added as a fifth managed service (Planned)
- **Timeline:** started 2026-10-20 19:36 CDT · finished 2026-10-20 19:37 CDT
- Request (Nick, 2026-10-20 19:37 CDT): "can we add OpenWebUI as a service feature that OCC can monitor-manage?"
- Scope: no new phase (nothing is built yet); the work folds into existing phases: schema fields in 03 (`metrics_source`, `available_check`, `lock_file`, `window`, `start_note`, LAN-visible badge), a Docker-container metrics source and helpers in 04, the catalogue entry and live checks in 05, the badge in 08, the threat-model note in 11; the Phase 10 candidate list no longer offers it.
- Grounding (verified 2026-10-20 19:37 CDT): `open-webui.service` is static (`docker start -a open-webui`, `Wants=prometheus-ollama.service`), Nick is in the `docker` group, the container exists (exited), port 8080 on host networking. Key finding: the unit's cgroup holds only the Docker client, so metrics must come from the container's cgroup (ADR-0011, spec R19).
- Decisions: spec A7 and R19, ADR-0011 (control the existing unit, mirror the toggle's window open/close, respect the toggle lock, never touch the container/unit/scripts/`Super + Alt + O`). Definition of done gained an Open WebUI item; "four services" → "five" throughout.

### 2026-10-21 05:57 CDT: Phase 04: Service adapters (✅ Complete)
- **Timeline:** started 2026-10-21 05:29 CDT (claim commit 99ff331) · finished 2026-10-21 05:57 CDT · merged 2026-10-21 06:00 CDT
- Built: `internal/systemd` (batched `systemctl --user show --timestamp=unix`, positive verb allowlist with unit-name check, `--no-block` start/stop/restart, `systemd-run` transient launcher with `Type=exec`), `internal/procscan` (user-only `/proc` scan, external instance = matching processes outside OCC's units plus their trees, totals, `/proc/net/tcp{,6}` port owner and LAN-visible check, `CgroupIO`, escalating `Stopper`), `internal/probe` (loopback-only HTTP health/busy with JSON paths, TCP, `LockHeld`), `internal/docker` (inspect, container cgroup metrics via the main pid, cached background `docker stats` fallback), `internal/logs` (journal/file tail with caps, ANSI stripping, `O_NOFOLLOW`; error counts in a window), `internal/hypr` (close windows by title, Lua dispatch), `internal/service` (`Controller` interface, `Manager` with concurrent deadline-bounded snapshots, stale views, CPU deltas, in-flight tracking, transient pre-checks, external stop/restart, window close; `Demo` with ten scripted services). ADR-0016 (`--no-block` + tracking), ADR-0017 (external stop rules), ADR-0018 (metrics sources, new packages); ADR-0005 flipped to Accepted with measured facts; ADR-0003 note (Go 1.27.3).
- Verified on the machine (ADR-0005): transient units survive their launcher; CPU and memory accounting work; **IO counters are never set for user units** (no `io` controller delegated), so IO comes from `/proc/<pid>/io` over `cgroup.procs`; `CPUAccounting=` is deprecated in systemd 262 and dropped; `--collect` unloads failed units; `Type=exec` turns a missing launcher into an error; SIGINT delivered; restart works on transient units. Read-only snapshot of docsync, Ollama, Open WebUI (+ `docker inspect`) and MM3: 129 ms, states match `systemctl is-active`.
- Deviations: two packages beyond the planned layout (`internal/docker`, `internal/hypr`; ADR-0018). `systemd-run` also gets `--quiet` and `-p Type=exec`, and not `CPUAccounting`. The lock reason is generic ("another program is acting on <name>"; no `lock_reason` field). MM3's busy path is `jobs.[].status` (verified in `jobs.py`; `waiting_for_input` exists and is for Phase 05 to classify). A transient unit that disappears without an OCC stop shows Distressed "exited" for `distress_window` (its real result is lost to `--collect`). **Go toolchain bumped 1.27.2 → 1.27.3** because `govulncheck` started failing on GO-2026-6809 (`crypto/x509`); host change documented in OSMods `Go Toolchain.md`.
- Follow-ups: Phase 05 decides `waiting_for_input`, drops the redundant Open WebUI `available_check`, verifies the container cgroup with Open WebUI running, and decides how a Docker MM3 shows (its processes belong to root, so `match` cannot see them). Phase 06 maps the `service` sentinel errors to HTTP codes and joins confirm texts/consumers from config. Phase 09: IO rates must clamp negative deltas; optionally read a vanished unit's exit status from the journal. All recorded in the later prompts.
- Tests: 301 test cases pass with `-race` (Phase 04 packages' coverage: systemd 99.3 %, procscan 96.4 %, probe 96.9 %, docker 98.4 %, logs 97.3 %, hypr 100 %, service 97.4 %); manager deadline test (a hung check costs only its own card), CPU deltas over two snapshots, fake `/proc` trees for scans, port owners, cgroup exclusion and process-group signalling. `go test -tags integration ./...` green on the machine (8 integration tests: five ADR-0005 checks, an end-to-end transient HTTP unit through the Manager, an external instance stopped and restarted as a unit, the read-only real snapshot), zero `occ-test-*` units left. `make check` green (gofmt, vet, golangci-lint 0 issues, tests, govulncheck clean). Markdown link check clean. No managed service was started, stopped or restarted; nothing audible.
